walkthrough:
Set up the composite function $fg(x) = (g(x))^2 + 1$ and equate to the form found in part (i):
$$(g(x))^2 + 1 = (2x + 3)^2 + 1$$

hints: The domain of $(fg)^{-1}$ is the range of $fg$ on $x > 0$.
walkthrough:
Set $y = (2x + 3)^2 + 1$ and rearrange to isolate $(2x + 3)^2$:
$$(2x + 3)^2 = y - 1$$

Take the positive square root since $x > 0$ implies $2x + 3 > 3$:
$$2x + 3 = \sqrt{y - 1} \implies 2x = \sqrt{y - 1} - 3 \implies x = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{y - 1} - \frac{3}{2}$$

Write the inverse function in terms of $x$:
$$(fg)^{-1}(x) = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{x - 1} - \frac{3}{2}$$

Determine the domain of $(fg)^{-1}(x)$, which is the range of $fg(x)$ for $x > 0$:
$$\text{For } x > 0:\quad fg(x) > (2(0) + 3)^2 + 1 = 10 \implies \text{Domain is } x > 10$$
